mission: Ben decides to follow the coordinates rather than report. The withholding he began with one omitted Force impression becomes a choice someone else names out loud.
why_now: The report to Luke is overdue. A seal is failing on an unreported clock. Wait for a committee or close the distance — the choice will not survive another day's delay.
conflict: Ben writes the honest report three times and deletes it three times. He can frame the delay as urgency — the seal will not wait — but what he is actually doing is closing the report before it leaves the ship. Desh watches him do it and will not let the choice stay unnamed.
turning_point: Desh leans over the copilot's shoulder, reads the first line, and says 'You're not sending that.' Ben's answer — 'Not yet' — is the first time the withholding is spoken aloud.
opening_hook: Ben's fingers are typing the report to Luke for the third time when Desh leans over the copilot's shoulder and reads the first line — 'You're not sending that'
closing_hook: Hyperspace entry toward uncharted coordinates. The wrongness does not diminish in hyperspace. It intensifies. They are heading toward the source.

stakes.personal: Ben chooses to act alone under cover of urgency — the pattern becomes visible to Desh before it becomes visible to Ben
stakes.interpersonal: Desh sees the pattern and follows anyway — loyalty enabling avoidance
stakes.external: Every hour of delay means more seal degradation

setting: Aboard the Steady Returns — cockpit, then hyperspace
sensory_details: The nav computer calculating a route through unmapped space; three deleted report drafts in the buffer; hyperspace blue through the viewport; the wrongness in the jump arriving as pressure against the bulkheads rather than fading with distance — it does not behave the way distance should
canon_elements_needed: Ben Skywalker institutional relationship with the Jedi Order
Post-Jacen Solo trust dynamics within the Skywalker family
Jedi mission reporting protocols and chain of command
Institutional withholding and secrecy in Jedi history
action_beats: Ben types and deletes his third draft of the report to Luke
Desh reads over Ben's shoulder and reaches across to the nav computer
Desh enters the uncharted fortress coordinates — the nav computer begins calculating a route through unmapped space
The Steady Returns jumps to hyperspace; the wrongness intensifies through the transition instead of fading
notes: Desh's quiet 'You're not reporting this' lands with the weight of someone who recognises institutional avoidance from inside. The two of them served in the same machine; he knows the signature. The withholding should be shown through action (deleted drafts, Desh's observation, hyperspace jump), not through an interior monologue explaining why Ben will not send it. Diagnostic-voice trap — if Ben reaches for an analysis of his own motives here, cut it. The reader should feel the omission before Ben names it to himself. Rotate the Force-wrongness metaphor for the hyperspace transition — not the handrail, not the note-played-flat; this scene's register is spatial (pressure against the bulkheads, the distance not behaving the way distance should).
